name: Donn Ua Duibne

attributes.attribute: wild boar that killed Diarmait Ua Duibne
killed by Diarmait at Ben Bulben after pricking him with a needle-sharp whisker
mother who bore the child to a shepherd lover
used by the shepherd to restore the crushed child as a pig

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Donn Ua Duibne is a mythological beast. This wild boar killed the hero Diarmait Ua Duibne. The boar was not truly a boar. It was a shape-shifting human. The boar was Diarmait's half-brother. His mother Cochrann bore him to her lover, a shepherd. Diarmait's father, also named Donn, learned of the child. The father crushed the infant to kill it. The shepherd knew magic. He waved a hazel wand over the mangled body. The child returned to life as a wild pig. The pig lived only for vengeance. Diarmait met him on the hill of Ben Bulben. The boar knew his chance had come. Diarmait killed the boar but lost his life. A needle-sharp whisker pricked the hero. Diarmait bled to death.

okr.objective: Records the wild boar Donn Ua Duibne, a shape-shifted half-brother whose vengeance killed the hero Diarmait.
key_results: Donn Ua Duibne was a wild boar, not an animal but a shape-shifting human.
He was Diarmait's half-brother, killed as an infant and revived as a pig by magic.
The boar met Diarmait on the hill of Ben Bulben.
Diarmait killed the boar but bled to death from a prick of its needle-sharp whisker.
